phases.notes: Measured live on wikipedia sandbox tab via chrome-bridge MCP: 500 console entries = 76,671 chars; 500 network entries = 2,331,618 chars (dropped:true, ring held 520). Network at limit=500 is ~30x console size, so count-based limit alone does NOT bound results — the byte ceiling is genuinely necessary. Grounding fact appended to decisions.md; patch surface untouched for phase 1.

Ceiling is a single ternary keyed on channel (MAX_CONSOLE_READ_RESULT_CHARS vs MAX_NETWORK_READ_RESULT_CHARS), each constant used exactly once; readConsoleMessages/readNetworkRequests both route through the same readCapture closure (no forked handler). resolveSince/resolveReadLimit/query/tabId lines unchanged and sit above the store call; the size check measures the exact result returned by captureStore.readConsole/readNetwork (the already-count-clamped CaptureRead). Pre-existing since/limit tests unchanged and pass. PassCriteria 1-3 met.

Both constants have JSDoc naming the measured live basis (console ~76,671 / network ~2,331,618 chars, 2026-09-04, en.wikipedia.org), the per-entry cap source (MAX_CONSOLE_TEXT_BYTES=8192 / MAX_BODY_PREVIEW_BYTES=4096), and state the cap bounds the whole serialised CaptureRead, not a single entry; placement/style match existing siblings.
